paper.title: An Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial Bandits with Arbitrary Delays

unmapped: Delays are arbitrary (non-uniform), chosen obliviously in advance, and unknown to the learner; delay d_s becomes known only when the observation arrives at s+d_s
All outstanding observations are revealed by the end of the game (t + d_t <= n)
settings.definition_quote: At time steps $t=1,\dots,n$ the learner picks actions $A_t\in[k]$ and immediately suffers the loss $\ell_{t,A_t}$, where $(\ell_t)_{t=1,\dots,n}$ are vectors in $[0,1]^k$. ... the environment chooses a sequence of delays $(d_t)_{t=1,\dots,n}$ and the player observes the tuples $(s,\ell_{s,A_s})$ for each $s$ such that $s+d_s = t$ at the end of round $t$. ... The learner has no prior knowledge of the quantities $n, D$, or $(d_t)_{t=1,\dots,n}$.

algorithms.name: FTRL for bandits with delay (hybrid 1/2-Tsallis + negative entropy regularizer), simple tuning
FTRL for bandits with delay with advanced tuning (Algorithm 2, skipping in learning rate)

conditions: t + d_t <= n for all t (all observations arrive by the end)

source.label: thm:simple
source.quote: The regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:FTRL-delay} with any non-increasing positive sequence of learning rates $(\eta_t)_{t=1,\dots,n}$ satisfies $\Reg_n\leq 4\sqrt{kn} + \eta_n^{-1}\log(k) + \sum_{t=1}^n \eta_t \mathfrak{d}_t$. In particular, the simple tuning $\eta_t^{-1} = \sqrt{2\mathfrak{D}_t/\log(k)}$ is proper and leads to a regret bound of $\Reg_n \leq 4\sqrt{kn} + \sqrt{8D\log(k)}$.

results.notes: Regret is E[sum loss of played] - min_i sum loss, oblivious adversary, so expected regret. The generic first statement (for arbitrary learning rates) is not recorded separately; it is a special case of Theorem 3 (general skipping-set bound) also not recorded.

symbols.min_skip: min over S subset of [n] of |S| + sqrt(D_{bar S} log K), where D_{bar S} is total delay of rounds not in S

conditions: t + d_t <= n for all t
tuning: advanced tuning of Algorithm 2: eta_t^{-1} = sqrt(tilde D_t / log k) with skipping of observations waiting longer than eta_t^{-1}

source.label: thm:adaptive
source.quote: \cref{alg:FTRL-delay} with advanced learning rate tuning provided in \cref{alg:eta} satisfies \begin{align*} \Reg_n &\leq 4\sqrt{kn}\\ &\quad + 10\max\begin{cases}\min_{S\subset[n]}|S|+\sqrt{D_{\bar S}\log(k)},\\ 2\log(k).\end{cases}\, \end{align*}

results.notes: Adaptive bound for unbalanced delays; no advance knowledge of delays.
